# About

I'm **Terry**, a mathematics student writing to understand: to follow an
idea carefully, test it against computation, and see what it reveals about
the world.

These notes are a record of questions pursued, arguments reconstructed, and
connections worth keeping.

:::

::: {.about-essay}

::: {.about-intro}

Mathematics is rigorous structure shaped by disciplined imagination. In a
proof, a symmetry, or an unexpected equivalence, precision can become a form
of art: a simpler way of seeing what was present all along.

:::

::: {.about-section data-index="01"}

## Mathematics as a way of seeing

Mathematics teaches me to look beneath complexity for structure. It asks for
clarity without sacrificing wonder, and it turns intuition into arguments
that can be examined, shared, and trusted.

What draws me most is its economy. A good definition gathers many examples
into one thought; a good proof makes the necessary feel inevitable. The
elegance lies not in ornament, but in how little remains once the right idea
has been found.

:::

::: {.about-section data-index="02"}

## Why mathematics

I chose mathematics because I wanted to study something closer to truth and
philosophy, not merely acquire one more technique. Techniques change with
their tools; a way of reasoning can continue to refine how one sees.

I have no illusion that I possess the effortless gifts of mathematical
prodigies. What I can bring is patience, seriousness, and a willingness to
stay with a difficult idea until a little more of its form becomes visible.

> There is only one heroism in the world: to see the world as it is, and to
> love it.
>
> [— Romain Rolland]{.quote-attribution}

For me, mathematics belongs to that effort: to look at reality without
simplifying away its difficulty, and still believe that it can be understood.

:::

::: {.about-section data-index="03"}

## From abstraction to the world

Abstraction matters most when it returns with sharper questions. I am
interested in computation, networks, probability, stochastic processes,
optimization, and modelling because they let mathematical ideas meet systems
that are uncertain, interconnected, and real.

This blog is both a workshop and a ledger: a place to reconstruct proofs,
test models, record numerical experiments, and preserve the moments when an
abstract idea suddenly explains something concrete.

:::
